rag.name: Finset.iSup_insert
rag.content:
theorem iSup_insert (a : α) (s : Finset α) (t : α → β) :
    ⨆ x ∈ insert a s, t x = t a ⊔ ⨆ x ∈ s, t x := by
  rw [insert_eq]
  simp only [iSup_union, Finset.iSup_singleton]

rag.name: Finset.iSup_union
rag.content:
theorem iSup_union {f : α → β} {s t : Finset α} :
    ⨆ x ∈ s ∪ t, f x = (⨆ x ∈ s, f x) ⊔ ⨆ x ∈ t, f x := by simp [iSup_or, iSup_sup_eq]

informal_statement: For any two subsets \( p \) and \( p' \) of a universal set \( M \), the image of their supremum under coercion to \( \text{Set } M \) is equal to the union of the two sets \( p \) and \( p' \).
informal_proof: The proof ensures that the supremum of \( p \) and \( p' \), when coerced to \( \text{Set } M \), corresponds precisely to the union of \( p \) and \( p' \). This follows directly from the properties of set operations and the definition of supremum within this context.

C1_dependencies.name: Set
C1_dependencies.content:
/-- A set is a collection of elements of some type `α`.

Although `Set` is defined as `α → Prop`, this is an implementation detail which should not be
relied on. Instead, `setOf` and membership of a set (`∈`) should be used to convert between sets
and predicates.
-/
def Set (α : Type u) := α → Prop
